body.rationale: Governing IPS is a draft, so I weight IPS compliance as provisional but still informative. I am maximum_diversification and cannot rank myself. I looked for portfolios the CIO can build from: ones that pass the hard limits, rest on the covariance structure, and survived review. Black-Litterman is first. It has no IPS breaches, 6.1 effective assets, and a backtest Sharpe of 0.70 with -21.2% drawdown. Its intra-category reviewer found its numbers consistent, and the one technical error, a mechanism claim about Omega, does not touch the weights. It also blends a market-equilibrium prior with views, which fits the covariance-led preference in a late-cycle regime. Resampled efficient frontier is second. It is the most diffuse compliant portfolio (13.3 effective assets) and has no breaches. Its weaknesses are thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%) and a gamma description that is inconsistent, but both are fixable. PC researcher is third. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the near-compliant portfolios (0.51), a backtest Sharpe of 0.70, and only -10.9% drawdown. It breaches volatility and tracking error, and reviewers noted the Sharpe floor and the rationale do not reconcile with the solved result. Even so, it is a useful middle-risk anchor that the compliant but high-drawdown portfolios lack. CVaR minimisation is fourth. It has no breaches and a backtest Sharpe of 0.74, and it brings a different, tail-aware view and is non-traditional, which helps family spread. Its reviewers flagged tuning to the edge of the volatility band and fitting to a few crises, which is a caution but not disqualifying. Max Sharpe is fifth. It has no breaches and a decent Sharpe, but the 46% concentration in us_value from one judged CMA gap is fragile. First beats fifth because Black-Litterman gets comparable return and Sharpe with much broader diversification (6.1 vs 3.8 effective assets) and a shallower drawdown (-21.2% vs -24.7%), without leaning on a single return gap. I flag market_cap_weight. It has the worst drawdown (-40.6%) and the highest CRO risk (0.80), it breaches the drawdown limit, and its reviewers found the ETF-AUM proxy invalid because it double-counts overlapping classes. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, which has value as an orthogonal diversifier despite its single-asset corner and three breaches.
